summary: Wenatchee NF summit: 1914 camp, 1929 D-6 cupola cabin, lookouts named to 1965, cabin removed or destroyed 1966. Hiking site today.

facts.status_note: Cabin removed (register, photo blog) or destroyed (firelookout.com) in 1966; no source describes a standing structure.

staffing.status: staffed in summers; lookouts named 1921 to 1965

access.note: Hike on foot to the summit. No closure or restriction is described in the pages read.

visit.trail_note: About 6 miles and 4,700 ft of gain from a trailhead 9.6 miles up paved Icicle Creek Road (FR 76), via the Fourth of July Creek Trail and Icicle Ridge Trail. The guide says a short rock climb reaches the top.

facts.remains_note: No page read describes footings or other remains on the summit today. The trail guide describes a bar sticking out of the summit and the former lookout site.

events.note: Newspaper account (October 12, 1928): a blasted-flat rock was to be the foundation for the lookout house
D-6 cupola cabin built; 48 loads of lumber packed up the trail by horse

Frank Allman named as Icicle Ridge lookout
New stairs and a catwalk built around the lookout house
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description calls the structure a tower; other accounts describe a cabin
Lookout still staffed at the time of a 1963 photo; Frank McWhirter named for 1963
Wayne Johnson named as lookout; last named lookout found
Register and photo blog say removed; firelookout.com says destroyed; WillhiteWeb says it lasted until 1966

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and firelookout.com put the site in Kittitas County; the Weebly county index lists Icicle Ridge under Chelan County. The record's Kittitas County is kept, and the story does not name a county.
Most accounts describe a D-6 cupola cabin built in 1929. A 1940 Coast and Geodetic Survey description calls the structure a tower. The story reports both and does not choose.
Four sources agree on 1966. The register and photo blog say removed; firelookout.com says destroyed. The story reports both words.

notes_for_editor: Kind 'ground' in the record kept: most accounts describe a cabin, but the 1940 Coast and Geodetic Survey description calls it a tower, so the tower question is open. Staffing names come from firelookout.com and newspaper transcriptions on the Weebly page; not checked against the originals. The 1932 fire item is a newspaper transcription on the Weebly page. One WebSearch was run; it added the posthaven blog. No current photos or site descriptions beyond the hike guide were found.
